purpose: Browsable survey of the settlement-building assets we actually hold or can source. Part 1 writes catalogue vibe/asset plans AGAINST this file so the province is designed for the breadth we own. Survey only: nothing here has been downloaded, extracted or kitted (that is item 6b).

pools.extracted: ONLY extracted-ground/ (51 MB of landscape textures). All 12.8k meshes are still inside Data1.rar (1.3 GB); all 24.6k textures inside Data2.rar (7.7 GB).
pools.note: Selective extraction against extract-list.txt is item 6b's first job. gitignored, never commit.

textures/architecture/{farmhouse,markarth,riften,solitude,whiterun,windhelm} are tropicalised repaints under VANILLA FILENAMES - they retexture the whole vanilla Imperial/Nord architecture set for free. No tropical architecture MESHES.

cultureRule.binding: material-culture.md: two Argonian building cultures are canon and regionally assigned. NEVER blend them in one settlement.

cultures.name: Shadowfen mud/wattle
cultures.description: wattle-and-daub over an exposed log skeleton; round or lumpy shells; walls sweat; sun-blessed mud; ground-level, not stilted

cultures.name: Murkmire reed/stilt
cultures.description: woven reed walls on wooden stilts; platforms extending high into the air, linked to one another, ascending from ground to hover over water and marsh; flexible buoyant timber causeways

cultures.name: Xanmeer (dead layer, not a living culture)
cultures.description: stepped stone pyramids linked by stone bridges; mazelike interiors; vakka-stone mechanisms; maintained as warnings, never inhabited in the modern style. Stone is a moral error post-Duskfall, so no modern Argonian building may read as stone.
cultures.regionHint: province-wide as ruin; densest in the deep interior

cultures.name: Imperial / foreign stone-and-timber
cultures.description: cut stone, mortar, sawn timber, tile and slate; foundations that sank in Murkmire soil; forts, docks, plantations, colonial civic buildings; concentrated where geography and history support it (Gideon, Blackwood, ports)
cultures.regionHint: west/north-west fringe, Topal Bay ports, road corridors

cultures.name: Culturally neutral
cultures.description: containers, tools, rope, rubble, fire, fish gear, generic furniture - readable in any culture's hands

cultures.name: Other foreign (Dunmer, Bosmer, Nord, Breton, Akaviri-flavoured)
cultures.description: use only where lore places these peoples: Dunmer border/Thorn, Bosmer/Valenwood fringe, Nord/Breton crews at ports. Never as a generic Argonian substitute.

gaps.title: No modular wattle-and-daub mud-hut kit
gaps.detail: One of the two canon Argonian building cultures rests on ~3 monolithic shells (hutexterior, argonianhouse, swamp house). Every Shadowfen village would be built from the same three meshes, which fails the anti-sameyness quota (no template over ~25% of a region's instances).
gaps.constrains: Shadowfen and all inland/northern settlement design
candidates: Mud Mother Grove - Argonian Mud Hut (SSE 146557)

gaps.title: No stepped-pyramid xanmeer exterior massing
gaps.detail: The Xanmeer Tileset's exterior is 9 pieces (wall, floor, corner, stairs, gazebo). Canon xanmeers are stepped pyramids linked by stone bridges. Only 11 whole mesoamerican statics (BM&V 22mjy + manny_gf pyramid) give the silhouette, and they have no interiors and no variation.
gaps.constrains: every xanmeer ruin, the deep-interior landmark layer, Hist chambers, the province's most distinctive skyline

gaps.title: No Argonian cultural props
gaps.detail: Zero grave-stake meshes in any pool. No crocodile-skull totems, plumage totems, reed mats, turtle-shell dishes, xeech'kis seed dolls, vossa-satl frog pipes, chime sets, egg-tender gear or Hist-sap items - the whole prop brief in material-culture.md.
gaps.constrains: POI recipe slot 3 (domestic props that narrate who lives here) for every Argonian place; grave-stakes fields as a place type
candidates: Wares of Tamriel and Argonian cultural-prop projects

gaps.title: No rafts, canoes or twin-hulled platform canoes
gaps.detail: Canon: personal rafts are the default vehicle; the small-draft doctrine; Riverback territory is navigable by small rafts and canoes and little else. Every hull we own is keeled and sailed - i.e. reads foreign. Moored boats are the commonest single prop in a marsh settlement, so this shows everywhere.
gaps.constrains: every waterside settlement, ferry stage, mooring and raft village; the travel-service graph's look
candidates: Skyrim Ferries (109843 - rafts and city ferries)

gaps.title: No causeway family
gaps.detail: Canon gives flexible partially-buoyant timber causeways and older stone-flagged causeways (Stormhold-Bogmother). We have arch bridges and plank bridges. The passerelles walkway kit + stockade scaffolding is a workable composite, but the buoyant/floating read has no asset.
gaps.constrains: inter-settlement links, the eight-city road network's marsh legs, floating villages
candidates: compose from citebosmer passerelles + stockade (no download needed)

gaps.title: Thin working/industrial props
gaps.detail: No fish-drying racks, salterns, kilns, reed-cutting gear, tanning frames for the marsh trades, moulting/grooming stations. The economy families in Part 1's taxonomy (saltern, fishery, kiln, logging, plantation) will otherwise all dress from the same generic barrel-and-crate pool.
gaps.constrains: the works taxonomy branch, economic legibility, distinctiveness between trade POIs
candidates: General Stores / clutter resources already in BM&V

gaps.title: No Hist tree asset
gaps.detail: The ~10 hero Hist (register kickoff hook) have no purpose-made mesh. Current best answer is BM&V's azura_tree02 monumental tree static plus the Phase 10 flora kit's largest composites. This decision is load-bearing for the look of every major settlement and should be settled at Part 6 for the first exemplar.
gaps.constrains: every Hist-centred settlement grammar, the province's spiritual centre

gaps.title: Tropical Skyrim has no architecture meshes
gaps.detail: Its textures/architecture folders are tropicalised repaints of the vanilla farmhouse and five city kits, under vanilla filenames. That is a free and valuable retexture path for the Imperial culture, but it adds no new building forms.
gaps.constrains: nothing, if the retexture path is used deliberately

gaps.title: The entire BM&V pool is still archived
gaps.detail: 12.8k meshes in Data1.rar and 24.6k textures in Data2.rar; only extracted-ground/ has been unpacked. Most families flagged have-unextracted above depend on a selective extraction pass against extract-list.txt.
gaps.constrains: item 6b kit builds; nothing in Parts 1-4

gaps.title: Fixtures without emitters
gaps.detail: The vanilla pool contains exactly one mesh categorised as light (the torch). Source-game illumination is engine light records plus a fixture mesh, so every lantern, brazier and campfire we place needs our renderer to supply the emitter and its budget.
gaps.constrains: night legibility and the settlement static-budget report

breadthWeOwn.conditionVariantCoverage: good for plank/shack (20 broken pieces), farmhouse (5 destroyed shells), xanmeer pottery (8 broken), rochester ruins, drowned ruins; POOR for mud huts (none) and docks (one)
breadthWeOwn.verdict: We can build stilt/boardwalk/dock/platform settlements and Imperial stone-timber towns to a high standard today. We cannot yet build a varied Shadowfen mud village, a monumental xanmeer skyline, or a mooring that reads Argonian.
